A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VeriEquivBench and the same core benchmark and evaluation pipeline. Their text, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and matchable. Internal inconsistencies in v2 can be assessed directly rather than representing unavailable evidence.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, code-transformation validation, RL baseline results, and an inspection of DafnySynthesis specifications.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports expanded transformation validation, additional evaluated models, and new failure-case analyses.

M1.justification: The autoformalization, tag-composition, code-refinement, bidirectional-equivalence, and back-translation procedures are retained, as are the GRPO auxiliary baselines. Expanded prompts and explanations do not establish a new algorithm, architecture, objective, or method component.

E1.justification: The benchmark datasets and principal tasks remain the same. Limited new scenario coverage appears in v2 Appendix E.3, which deliberately removes connectivity postconditions to test translation and judging of a partially incomplete specification. The newly highlighted 1,678 synthetic problems do not establish a new corpus: both versions already describe generating 1,893 candidates and retaining 215 annotated examples.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates Claude-4-sonnet, GPT-5, and Gemini-2.5-flash on end-to-end generation. v2 Appendix G.2 and Figure 23 additionally evaluate DeepSeek-R1, Qwen-2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct, and Llama3-70B alongside them, substantially expanding the comparison to open models.

E3.justification: Python-to-Dafny validation expands from 20 randomly sampled programs in v1 Section 5.1 to 1,011 selected programs, of which 648 execute successfully, in v2 Section 4.1 and Appendix G.1. This substantially changes the validation sample and documents a 30-minute compilation cutoff. Appendix E.3 also introduces controlled postcondition deletion. Newly disclosed sampling hyperparameters do not establish changed settings for existing experiments.

E4.justification: New Appendices E and F examine missing proof clauses, verifier sensitivity to equivalent precondition formulations, weak versus stronger specifications, deleted connectivity conditions, code-intent mismatches, and generated-test defects. These substantially broaden the failure analysis beyond v1's benchmark-specification inspection. That earlier inspection and the RL training curves remain in Appendix G.

E5.justification: The pass@4 reporting convention and point-estimate training curves are retained. Neither version reports independent-seed replication, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 reports 530/648 programs passing all transformation tests, or 81.79%, replacing the 90% result from v1's 20-program sample under expanded sampling. It adds open-model and case-study results and removes v1 Appendix D.1's 86.68% autoformalization passing-rate table. Its introduction and Figure 23 report zero exact matches, while Section 4.3 reports GPT leading equivalence at 2.65%; v1 instead highlights Claude's 4.83% exact matching and 10.34% equivalence. However, v2 Figure 5 retains v1's nonzero results, leaving these reports unreconciled.

T1.justification: The bidirectional-equivalence reasoning and Max checker remain substantively unchanged, with no new theorem, proof, or formal assumption. The original DafnySynthesis specification repairs are retained. New code examples support empirical failure analyses rather than introducing a different mathematical framework.

C1.justification: The principal ground-truth-free metric and 2,389-example benchmark contributions remain. The introduction strengthens the headline difficulty claim from Claude succeeding on 4.83% to failing on all instances, explicitly advertises 1,678 additional synthetic problems, and emphasizes user clarification through back-translation. These refine the contribution claims without replacing their central purpose.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantial interpretations involving verifier limitations, simplified implementations that satisfy formal checks while missing user intent, and difficulty generating code and specifications jointly. Appendix E.4 questions the reliability of co-generated unit tests, while Appendix F distinguishes code defects from invalid tests. These extend v1's emphasis on problem complexity and incomplete specifications, although some supporting judge explanations are mismatched to their examples.

D1.justification: v2 adds prompts for specification translation, LLM judging, and NL-to-Dafny generation in C.3-C.5. Appendix D discloses temperature/top-p settings of 0.7/0.9 for initial specification generation and 0.5/0.8 elsewhere, plus the rollout-processing sequence. G.1 adds datatype-conversion and timeout details. Conversely, v1's explicit autoformalization-filtering disclosure and per-question validation records disappear. Code and dataset access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes the Jiang et al. Draft, Sketch, and Prove reference and its associated translation-asymmetry motivation. Positioning against Clover, DafnyBench, and specification-comparison approaches otherwise remains largely unchanged. The two AlphaCode bibliography entries in v2 describe an already cited work rather than an additional research contribution.

P1.justification: v2 removes v1's duplicated Evaluation Metrics and Tasks section, consolidating the methodological narrative. It also rewrites portions of the contribution and results discussions and substantially reorganizes the appendices into named prompt subsections, model settings, qualitative analyses, synthesis examples, and retained experimental details. This is a substantial structural revision despite extensive retained prose.

P2.justification: v2 adds the six-model chart in Figure 23 and numerous prompt, failure-case, and synthesis-code displays in Figures 10-22. It replaces v1's per-program transformation table with an aggregate error breakdown, removes the duplicated Max figure, and reformats prompt displays and typography. Existing diagrams and repair examples are largely retained; v1 Figure 6 is reproduced as v2 Figure 5.

improvement.justification: The larger transformation-validation sample, additional model comparisons, expanded prompt/settings documentation, and removal of duplicated prose improve evidence and inspectability. However, v2 introduces unresolved central performance contradictions between Figure 5 and its introduction/Figure 23. Moreover, the judge explanations in Appendices E.2 and E.4 discuss different problems from their accompanying examples, weakening validation of the central evaluation pipeline. These material benefits and reliability problems prevent a confident net quality judgment.
